programme: TFDP1 (DP1, obligate E2F dimerization partner driving CDKN1A, MYC, RB1, CCNA2, PCNA), KAT5 (Tip60, the catalytic subunit of the NuA4 acetyltransferase complex — its own target list recovers its complex partners TRRAP, EP400, ACTL6A, H2AZ1 — which acetylates p53/p73 and CDKN1A), and YY1 (a broad chromatin-associated integrator whose targets include TP53 and MYC) converge on the same small checkpoint gene set — CDKN1A, TP53, MYC, RB1 — shared pairwise across their three independently-inferred target lists. That convergence, not any one factor alone, is what makes this a recognisable module: an E2F/DP1-RB proliferation switch coupled to Tip60-mediated p53/chromatin acetylation, with YY1 as a shared cofactor at the same loci.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, this axis is documented piecemeal rather than as one dataset: KAT5 is reported altered alongside oxidative stress and senescence markers in a neuronal infection model (PMID 34571838), and TFDP1-adjacent cell-cycle/MYC-network genes are disturbed by a SARS-CoV-2 accessory protein acting through the related MGA/MAX complex in a cardiomyocyte model (PMID 36180527). Together they point to infected or virally stressed cells being pushed toward a DNA-damage/senescence-like checkpoint response rather than proliferation; no source here places YY1 in COVID-19 specifically.
role_in_b: In ovarian cancer the same three factors are each independently placed: TFDP1 drives cell-cycle progression downstream of ZNF146 (PMID 38614125), KAT5 supports PD-L1-mediated immune evasion (PMID 35392432), and YY1 recurs across four papers — angiogenesis via HIF1A (PMID 41072350), drug-resistance signalling (PMID 40867514), ferroptosis suppression via USP43 (PMID 40890129), and metabolic/angiogenic reprogramming under bevacizumab resistance (PMID 42134086). Here the module is read as co-opted for checkpoint escape and immune evasion rather than arrest.
shared_axis: The same E2F/DP1-RB–Tip60–YY1 checkpoint module appears to be engaged in both settings but driven toward opposite outputs: arrest/senescence in virally stressed cells versus proliferative, immune-evasive escape in the tumour. That is consistent with a generic DNA-damage/chromatin checkpoint machinery being reused by an acute viral stressor in one disease and subverted by a chronic malignancy in the other, rather than any COVID-19-specific or ovary-specific biology.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the target-list overlap alone (CDKN1A/TP53/MYC/RB1 shared by TFDP1, KAT5 and YY1), and two of the three carrying factors are independently placed in ovarian cancer by multiple papers, with KAT5 and TFDP1 each touched by one COVID-19 paper. But no source states the two diseases share this axis together, YY1 has no COVID-19 citation at all despite a mid-range OT score, and the TFDP1 COVID-19 paper concerns an adjacent complex (MGA/MAX) rather than DP1-E2F directly — so the cross-disease link is inference from two separately-documented halves, not a retrieved joint claim.
support: PMID 34571838 — KAT5 altered alongside oxidative stress/senescence in a COVID-19 neuronal model; PMID 36180527 — SARS-CoV-2 Nsp6 perturbs the MGA/MAX complex adjacent to TFDP1's network in a cardiomyocyte model; PMID 38614125 — TFDP1 drives cell-cycle progression downstream of ZNF146 in ovarian cancer cells; PMID 35392432 — KAT5 supports PD-L1 expression in ovarian cancer, suppressed by aspirin; PMID 41072350 — YY1/HIF1A modulates ovarian cancer angiogenesis; PMID 40867514 — YY1 as a central node in ovarian cancer drug-resistance pathways; PMID 40890129 — YY1-induced USP43 suppresses ferroptosis in ovarian cancer; PMID 42134086 — lactylation-driven bevacizumab resistance tied to the same angiogenic/metabolic programme YY1 sits in.
how_to_falsify: Knock down KAT5 in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells and in an ovarian cancer line (e.g. the PD-L1-linked model from PMID 35392432) side by side, and read out CDKN1A/TP53 acetylation and induction: if the infected cells show no p53/CDKN1A checkpoint activation while the tumour line loses PD-L1 as expected, the two settings are not running the same Tip60-checkpoint module and the shared-axis claim fails. A second, independent test: silence TFDP1 in both systems and check whether the same E2F target genes (MYC, RB1, CCNA2, PCNA) move together — divergent target-gene behaviour would falsify the claim that this is one reused module rather than two coincidentally overlapping factor sets.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood versus ovary — an acute systemic viral infection compared with a solid gonadal tumour — so any shared axis is necessarily a generic stress/checkpoint mechanism, not tissue-specific biology. Support is drawn from 64 patient-group comparisons but only 4 independent cohort pairs, so replication is modest. Notably E2F2 itself — TFDP1's canonical dimerization partner — was removed as tissue-generic (percentile 0.929), which is why the account can only point to TFDP1 and not the E2F factors directly; this is the documented reason for its absence, not an oversight. The single-view list (AKNA, GFI1, TCF20, etc.) and the tissue-generic list (NFATC1, HLX, SREBF2, TWIST1, RUNX2, PRDM1, BCL3, and the duplicate GFI1 entry, among others) were both checked and none of them figure in this account. THRA, AIRE, ZNF256 and ZNF202 have no usable citations in either disease and are excluded from the programme entirely rather than forced in; RARG and NR5A1 have solid ovarian-cancer-only citations but nothing placing them in COVID-19 despite RARG's very high COVID-19 OT percentile (0.955), and FOXP4 has the strongest single-factor cross-disease citation record of the whole set (three long-COVID GWAS papers plus one ovarian-cancer Wnt/PTK7 paper) but regulates only its own FOXP1/FOXP2 paralogs, so it does not integrate into a multi-factor module and is left out of this account rather than stretched to fit.
